Event: `e790acd298945d2da74299976d3aa382` · 2026-10-16T21:37:37Z

> Q9 (steward-latency needs a reset to dump the trace). The kernel prints its scheduler trace only in `system_reset` (kernel/src/redoubt.rs:158), and the oracle refuses a log without `SCHED-TRACE-END` (sched_oracle.rs:204) and needs the trace for R10 and the audits. Under the real init nothing resets at a steward case's end: init resets only on a refusal or the reboot rule (init.rs:153, :302); the stand-in resets itself from init's place. So the real-steward case cannot be judged as the brief says without a way to end its boot in a reset.
> 
> Default: inside the same `latency-probe` feature, a steward that finds the file `latency-done` in the console principal's home at its start exits at once (code 9, as restart-probe's); alice's session writes that file as the case's last step; six such exits within 60 s trip init's reboot rule, whose `system_reset` dumps the trace before the reboot (steward-restart-reboot's path; the case's expectations end at `init: rebooting` and `SCHED-TRACE-END`). Nothing of init or the kernel moves; the host test that nothing but the case's recipe enables the feature covers it too; steward.md names it beside the probe's other test-only behaviour. Alternatives: (b) an init test-only power-off, (c) the oracle judging without a trace from the steward's own `destroy_call` bracket (more than the prefix change). I take (a) unless you say otherwise.
> 
> Cost note for later: each boot starts 21 spinner VMs and 40 probe leases under icount; I will measure the first run before the sweep and report its length with the 1..20 sweep's projection.

On the first run, count the entries after the marker against the ring's capacity; if the window is not whole, fall back to (c) for R10 only, which then is recorded, not judged (destroy_call is call-to-return, not R10's kernel time), with the page saying so beside the table. (b) is refused: init gains no test feature for a measurement the steward can trigger.
>

### Architect · Answer

Event: `19bc88442d8074cf258cf2fa90537c6e` · 2026-10-16T22:07:46Z

> Q10: accepted, with the bounding sentence (appended to .wash/local/STEWARD4-ruling.md). The check counts domains that use a volume; the steward holds a vault's root badge only to mint each session's connection in that session's scope (R41), so the user is the session, not the steward. users() and the endpoint rule skip an exempt server; host tests both ways as proposed; alice's net leaves the confined manifest.
> 
> Yes to your question: the exemption is safe not by itself but because two walls hold independently of init's count, and init.md must say so in the same breath so nobody reads it as "the steward may route any endpoint to any set": (1) the steward binds a labelled volume only to a session in exactly that volume's label set (its binding rule, checked by the model's routes and the vault's exact_labels guard); (2) the server it mints at admits only a caller whose labels equal its volume's (R25), so a steward that routed a labelled endpoint to another set would be refused by the server it routed to; and the steward never reads a vault itself, a declassification reads through a crossing carrying the item's labels (R42). The exact sentence for init.md 'The confinement check' is in the file.
